body:
For the same-host setup in this report, try launching from project B with an explicit working directory:

```sh
codex --remote unix:// --cd "$PWD"
```

When the server is on another machine, use an absolute project path that exists on that server, not the client's `$PWD`. A relative `--cd` is resolved on the server.

Tracing new-thread startup at commit `112be0bd74ce327788613f4f8f92e8b7c92447c7` points to deliberate server-owned cwd selection rather than a hooks-specific substitution:

- [Explicit `--remote`, including a Unix socket, selects `AppServerTarget::Remote`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/112be0bd74ce327788613f4f8f92e8b7c92447c7/codex-rs/tui/src/lib.rs#L916-L943). This differs from implicit local-daemon reuse.
- [The cwd helper](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/112be0bd74ce327788613f4f8f92e8b7c92447c7/codex-rs/tui/src/app_server_session.rs#L2067-L2078) forwards only an explicit remote override in that mode. Without `--cd`, the new-thread request omits cwd.
- [Server configuration](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/112be0bd74ce327788613f4f8f92e8b7c92447c7/codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs#L1452-L1457) defaults to the server process directory when no cwd override is supplied and resolves relative overrides there. The [SessionStart hook request](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/112be0bd74ce327788613f4f8f92e8b7c92447c7/codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs#L151-L159) copies `turn_context.cwd`.

There are already [unit tests for omission and explicit forwarding](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/112be0bd74ce327788613f4f8f92e8b7c92447c7/codex-rs/tui/src/app_server_session.rs#L3006-L3202): `thread_lifecycle_params_omit_cwd_without_remote_override_for_remote_sessions` and `thread_lifecycle_params_forward_explicit_remote_cwd_override_for_remote_sessions`. They assert that start/resume/fork omit cwd without an override and forward `repo/on/server` unchanged when it is explicit.

A focused improvement would be to clarify the `--remote` and `--cd` help text: explicit remote sessions use server-side cwd semantics, so a new thread needs `--cd` to select another project. I would not change hook payloads or automatically forward the client's local directory, since that path may not exist remotely.

Verification boundary: the original upstream filtered suite was attempted with Rust 1.95.0, just and cargo-nextest installed in isolation, but compilation did not finish within the bounded attempt. No unit tests passed or failed because none ran. I have not verified live daemon hooks or `thread/list` behavior end to end.

Thanks — I verified this with real Codex 0.152.1 and 0.153.4 clients on macOS arm64.

With the daemon started in A, explicit `--remote unix://` launched from B uses A consistently in hooks, thread metadata, and actual shell execution. Adding an absolute `--cd B` makes all three use B.

Ordinary LocalDaemon startup preserves B, and native queue delivery works there too. We have updated our integration to use that path.

My original report therefore needs a diagnosis correction: the observed directory difference is real, but hooks accurately report the thread’s actual cwd. Clearer `--remote` / `--cd` help would address the surprising behavior.
